newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy, Netherlands say EMU timetable must be met.
newsitem.headline: Italy, Netherlands say EMU timetable must be met.

text.p: Italy and the Netherlands agreed on Wednesday that the current timetable for planned European economic and monetary union (EMU) and linked EU legislation must be respected, the two countries said in a joint statement.

Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco held brief talks with Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm on Wednesday and agreed to a string of resolutions over the creation of a single European currency.
"These resolutions mark an important step forward in the construction of an economic and monetary union based on a stable ero," the statement said.

The three men said the single currency, due to be launched in 1999, had to be strong and stable to strengthen the single market, improve employment prospects and boost the competitiveness of the European economy.
"It was also agreed that it is necessary to strengthen the procedures of the EU budget in order to enhance the discipline and accountablility of the budget process," the statement said.
The statement stressed the need to fulfill existing timetables for the launch of EMU and the creation of a grid for EU currencies left outside the euro umbrella.
"Any delay with respect to the starting date of the third stage (of EMU)...would jeopardise the credibility of the process," the statement said.
The three ministers noted with satisfaction the progress all member countries were making to meet Maastrich Treaty criteria.

Ciampi and Visco confirmed that the Italian government's main goal was to ensure that Italy became a founding member of EMU. Earlier, Ciampi told reporters he was convinced Italy would make the grade.
The Italian government announced on Wednesday it was preparing a mini-budget to ensure it respected the terms of the Maastricht Treaty. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
